title: Build an accessible landing page structure
description: Use the existing stack and semantic HTML to define a clear page flow.
prompt:
Act as a web developer.

Task: Build an accessible landing page structure.

Input context:
- OFFER: [OFFER]
- AUDIENCE: [AUDIENCE]
- PRIMARY ACTION: [PRIMARY ACTION]
- STACK: [STACK]

Use the existing stack and semantic HTML to define a clear page flow. Include responsive behaviour, form validation, status feedback and acceptance checks. Avoid unnecessary dependencies and distinguish proposed copy from verified facts.

Preserve the existing architecture, minimise dependencies and define scope, acceptance criteria and relevant tests. Keep secrets server-side. No production changes or deployment without approval.

Use English for explanations unless the task or user explicitly requires another language. Use clear sections and a format suited to the deliverable. If essential information is missing, ask a focused question before concluding. Label assumptions and unknowns. Do not invent facts, sources, results or completed checks. End with verification criteria and remaining limitations.
exampleResult:
## Workshop page outline
Use a meaningful heading, programme section, confirmed terms and a labelled enquiry form. Errors identify the field and preserve valid values. On mobile, content follows a logical reading order rather than two narrow columns. Keyboard, zoom and server-response checks still need execution; this outline is not proof of accessibility conformance.
useCases: Prepare a reviewable deliverable: build an accessible landing page structure.
Compare assumptions, evidence and practical next steps before taking action.
tips: Provide concrete, authorised context for offer before using this prompt.
